map.rationale: Main nave and tower wall fields show irregular rounded pebble masonry with random coursing — the rough cobble read, not dressed blocks.
Tower corners, gable rakes and the projecting pilasters along the nave are crisp, regularly-coursed lighter dressed blocks — kept distinct from the rounded cobble wall they frame.
A continuous neat ashlar band runs along the ground course and again where wall meets roof — straight-coursed dressed stone, unlike the cobble above it.
Steep nave gable and the pyramidal tower cap are warm dark-brown horizontal timber planking — strong grain contrast against the grey stone.
The tall 1×3 windows are framed by smooth, fine-grained pale-grey stone with no coursing lines — a third grey, finer than both cobble and stone-brick.
Each window recess reads as a flat dark void set behind the pale frame — the deep shadowed glazing within the surround.

entry.rationale: The arched opening at the tower base shows a vertical-plank dark timber door, matching the roof's warm brown wood tone.
